subject: Readout & Architecture Session: ownership of throughput window
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@nimbushealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Readout & Architecture Session: ownership of throughput window

Hi Alex / team,

Thanks for lining up the pilot — we want to run a combined architecture deep-dive + performance readout so everyone has context before the hands-on load tests. Proposed objectives:
- Walk architecture decisions that affect token throughput (KV cache priming, batching, routing policies)
- Present the benchmark matrix and observed p50/p95 latencies for recent runs
- Agree on a load-test window: sustained targets, warmup behavior, and fallback policies

Initial proposal: 90–120 minute session with dedicated 45-minute readout followed by a 30–45 minute Q&A / runbook alignment. Suggested slots (US/EAST friendly):
- Tue 2028-09-19 10:00–12:00 ET
- Wed 2028-09-20 14:00–16:00 ET

Target throughput for the readout: 20k tokens/sec sustained across the cluster (1-minute windows) with p95 generation latency goal < 300ms for 128-token streams; we'll show recent dry-run numbers in the attached benchmark_plan_v2.pdf and load_test_matrix.xlsx.

Please confirm preferred slot and attendee list.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Staff Product Manager, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Attachments: benchmark_plan_v2.pdf (plan + expected metrics)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@nimbushealth.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Readout & Architecture Session: ownership of throughput window

Jonas —

Thanks for the draft. Either slot works for me but prefer Wed 9/20 because infra needs a little more time to finalize the Dedicated reservation. A couple of notes for the readout so we can keep it actionable:
- Split the meeting into two discrete blocks on the calendar: (1) architecture/decisions (45m) (2) benchmark readout + ops checklist (45m). That way external stakeholders can join only what’s relevant.
- We should reserve a dedicated pool for the 20k tokens/sec target to avoid noisy neighbors; I'll open the runbook_reservations.csv and mark the capacity request (GPU pool: 6 x A100 equivalent).
- Warmup: plan for 10 minutes of prefix priming and KV-cache warming; we'll show the effects on p95 across 1/5/15 minute buckets.

Attendees from our side: Irene (Infra), Dylan (Perf), Karthik (Serving).

I attached the current load_test_matrix.xlsx with permutations and the expected measurement columns.

Irene Choi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
irene.choi@redwood.com

Attachments: load_test_matrix.xlsx

Date: Thu, 14 Sep 2028 09:01:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Readout & Architecture Session: ownership of throughput window

Quick technical checklist before we lock the calendar:
- Capacity: ops, please provision a dedicated 6-GPU pool (A100-equivalent) for a 90-minute window + 30m tear-down. I'll submit the reservation in the infra portal but want a manual confirmation from ops.
- Warmup priming: run 10min of synthetic prefix traffic at 5k tokens/sec to populate KV caches, then ramp to the 20k sustained target in 3 steps (25%, 50%, 100%).
- Metrics: collect token emit rate, GPU utilization, internal batching stats, queue size, and per-request p95; store traces in the sprint bucket (retention 30d).
- Fallback: define a 2-tier fallback — (A) reduce quantization to perf variant, (B) route to warm spare region (us-west-2).

I attached runbook_reservations.csv with the reservation template and tagging. Also: Dylan, can you bring the most recent dry-run graphs?

Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving Architecture
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: runbook_reservations.csv
